newsitem.title: UK: Southern electricity solo after York's bid.
newsitem.headline: Southern electricity solo after York's bid.

text.p: Britain's electricity sector lost Yorkshire to a 1.5 billion pound ($2.4 billion) U.S. bid on Monday, leaving just Southern Electric the only remaining independent regional electricity company (Rec) of the 12 set up at privatisation.
Yorkhire is the seventh to be bought by an American company.
In its place, Energy Group made its market debut after demerger from Hanson Plc , but analysts said it didn't have the attractions of a Rec for a predator.
"This clearly throws Southern into play but Energy is too big, too diverse," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Yorkshire agreed to the 927 pence per share bid from U.S. companies American Electric Power Co Inc and Public Service Co of Colorado, saying it was at a multiple of 11.3 times earnings per share before exceptionals on the year.
The current Conservative government has only blocked two bids for Recs -- from generators National Power and PowerGen .
It has waved through all previous U.S. bids along with two by water companies, one from Scottish Power and Hanson's takeover of Eastern Electricity, now part of Energy Group.

But a general election is due by May 22 and the opposition Labour party, favourites to win, might be less amenable to Yorkshire's takeover, analysts said, as there are concerns about reciprocity for UK firms in the U.S. and it could hamper the ability to draw comparisons for regulation.
"Not everybody thinks it's going to go through ... That's what the (share) price is saying to us," Marshall Whiting of SocGen said.
Yorkshire's shares were trading at 879 pence, up 60-1/2 pence, by 1300 GMT, some way below the bid price.
Southern gained 24-1/2 pence to 771 pence, as its now unique attractions were tempered by the price tag of over two billion pounds which analysts attached.
"Southern now has scarcity value but there are not that many companies that could afford it," the analyst said.

The cash-rich Recs have proved a happy hunting ground for U.S. firms which also see benefits in Britain's relatively relaxed regulatory system and the possibility of cost savings, but analysts said Southern might prove to large to swallow.
Southern has already had its own plans for a merger with generator National Power thwarted by the government, and its proposed takeover of neighbouring water company Southern Water was also blocked.
It has now said it intends to stay independent.

Analysts said on a similar valuation to Yorkshire, Southern would cost around 880 pence per share but added that this could be lower because it lacked the attractions of a telecommunications interest to match Yorkshire's 20 percent stake in Ionica.
"We would be looking in the mid-800 pence per share," the analyst said.

Other companies in the sector are unlikely to prove as attractive as the Recs have, analysts said, with some, including generators National Power and PowerGen, protected by a controlling special share held by the government.
Ironically, Energy, which debuted on the market on Monday, owns former Rec Eastern Electricity.

But the company, the last part of conglomerate Hanson to be spun off under its four-way demerger, also has large U.S. coal and generation interests, which could deter predators both through size and spread of interests, analysts said.

And although analysts said bidders might turn the spotlight on water utilities, takeovers in that sector are automatically referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), which is likely to deter interest.
"We've pretty much had it now. It was the Recs which were attractive, they carried virtually no regulatory or political concerns," Whiting said.
($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
